patterns.rule: The stem is found by removing **-en** and checking the final consonant. Add **-t** for 2nd/3rd singular.
patterns.subtitle: Dutch weak verbs in -en: stem + ending, with -t for jij/hij/zij.

concepts.label: Nevenschikkend
concepts.labelGloss: joins two main clauses; the verb stays in second place (en, maar, of, want, dus, doch)
concepts.explainer:
A **nevenschikkend voegwoord** joins two main clauses, each of which could stand alone. After it, the second clause keeps **normal word order**: the subject, then the conjugated verb in second place.

There are only six. Learn them by heart, because every other conjunction works differently:

**en · maar · of · want · dus · doch**

| Clause 1 | | Clause 2, verb second |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ik ben moe, | **want** | ik **heb** hard gewerkt. |
| Het regent, | **maar** | wij **gaan** toch fietsen. |
| Ga je mee, | **of** | **blijf** je thuis? |

> The conjunction itself sits *outside* the clause. Read the clause after it as if it were a sentence on its own: *ik heb hard gewerkt*.

**Dus** can also be an adverb, and then the verb jumps forward: *dus **ga** ik naar bed*. Both are correct. As a conjunction it keeps the order: *dus ik **ga** naar bed*.

:::order{sentence="Ik ben moe, want ik heb hard gewerkt." after="want" en="I'm tired, because I've worked hard."}
:::

concepts.label: Onderschikkend
concepts.labelGloss: starts a bijzin; the conjugated verb goes to the end (omdat, als, dat, hoewel)
concepts.explainer:
An **onderschikkend voegwoord** starts a **bijzin**, a clause that can't stand on its own. Inside the bijzin the conjugated verb moves to **the very end**.

**omdat · als · dat · of** *(whether)* **· hoewel · toen · terwijl · voordat · nadat · zodat · zodra · tenzij · totdat · sinds**

| Main clause | | Bijzin, verb last |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ik ben moe, | **omdat** | ik hard **heb gewerkt**. |
| Ik blijf thuis | **als** | het morgen **regent**. |
| Ik denk | **dat** | hij morgen **komt**. |

With two verbs at the end, both orders are fine: *omdat ik hard **heb gewerkt*** or *omdat ik hard **gewerkt heb***.

When the bijzin comes first, the main clause starts with its verb:

***Omdat** ik moe **ben**, **ga** ik vroeg naar bed.*

> **Want or omdat?** Both mean *because*. **Want** leaves the verb where it is: *want ik **ben** moe*. **Omdat** sends it to the end: *omdat ik moe **ben***.

:::order{sentence="Ik ga vroeg naar bed, omdat ik erg moe ben." after="omdat" en="I'm going to bed early, because I'm very tired."}
:::

concepts.label: Tegenstelling
concepts.labelGloss: the next statement pushes against the last one (echter, toch)

concepts.label: Oorzaak
concepts.labelGloss: the next statement explains why (daarom, immers)

concepts.label: Toevoeging
concepts.labelGloss: the next statement adds to the last one (bovendien, ook)

concepts.label: Volgorde
concepts.labelGloss: ordering in time or argument (eerst, vervolgens, ten slotte)
